The grid resolver's premise: instead of an agent writing an "intent" file that a program routes and hopes reads well, the agent places every element on a literal topological grid — cards, edge paths, edge labels — cell by cell, so the input is a low-fidelity rendering of the output. Yes. Delegate each image read to a subagent (the `Agent` tool). The subagent reads the PNG and returns a short text verdict. Only that text stays in the main conversation — the base64 image data stays in the subagent's context, which is thrown away after it replies.

Trade-off: the image tokens still get spent once, in the subagent. The saving is that they do not sit in the main session and compound across every later turn — which is what pushed the forked session to 920,805 cached tokens.

27	A single-hop model check recovers only 6% to 11% of an invalidation chain. There is no way

card werk-card-blind  [decided]
The open-card announcement has no recovery path once it drops from context
why: This session's whole visible conversation ran with the map open at #pr-logic. I was never told, because lastCard in agent.ts is state in the long-lived server process, set before my visible context began. There is no tool for the agent to ask which card is open right now.

src/agent.ts's send() sent describe() only when the open card changed (per #werk-pane). If the change happened before the agent's visible context — a resumed session, or a turn dropped by compaction — the agent had no way to learn or re-derive the open card. That happened this session: the pane sat on #pr-logic the whole time and the agent never knew.

Fixed: send() now always prepends something when a card is open. The full describe() block still fires only on change; every other turn gets tag(), a one-line '[still on #id — title]' reminder cheap enough to send always. AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md now say 'this card' or 'current' defaults to whatever that line names, unless Eryk gives a different id.

Verified: bun build src/agent.ts compiles clean.
